item.title: CVE-2026-115207 [CVSS:3.1 5.5 MEDIUM]
item.description:
A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve arbitrary file creation outside the intended working directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected. Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary locations with the permissions of the executing user.

item.title: CVE-2026-93653 [CVSS:3.1 5.5 MEDIUM]
item.description:
A denial of service flaw was found in Poppler's Splash backend. A crafted PDF with tiling-pattern geometry approaching the int32 boundary can cause SplashOutputDev::tilingPatternFill to compute an attacker-controlled repeat count that drives an excessively long loop in the pattern-fill scanline routine, without a corresponding memory allocation. An attacker could exploit this by supplying a malicious PDF to an application that renders it via Poppler's Splash backend, causing the rendering process to consume 100% CPU for an attacker-controlled, extended duration.
Score: 5.5 (MEDIUM) Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

item.title: CVE-2026-134129 [CVSS:4.0 8.7 HIGH]
item.description:

item.title: CVE-2026-122093
item.description:
Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.
The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.
An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.
